_doc: Car system / component → AI / orchestration / business concept. Use for technical analogies. Each entry has the car concept, what it maps to in AI, and a one-line punchline ready to deploy.

mappings.punchline: Different engines for different jobs. Honda K-series for daily reliability, LS swap for cheap horsepower, Ferrari V12 for sound. Same with models.

mappings.ai_concept: Foundation IDE + base platform (Claude Code, Cursor, custom app)
mappings.punchline: Engine swaps are easy. Chassis swaps are a rebuild. Pick your platform once.
1,000 horsepower at the crank means nothing if the drivetrain can't put it to the wheels.
Cheap suspension over a pothole and the whole car shakes. Bad error handling in one workflow and the whole stack panics.
Brakes don't make you faster. They let you go faster, because you know you can stop.

mappings.ai_concept: Tools (the AI's actual interface to the world)
mappings.punchline: Wrong tires = wrong performance. Doesn't matter what's under the hood.
Every modern car problem is an electrical problem. Same with every modern AI problem.
The ECU doesn't make horsepower. It tells horsepower when to show up.
The PCM coordinates the engine, transmission, and everything else. The orchestrator does the same for subagents.
Wrong TCM tune and you ride the wrong gear forever.
The body control module runs the lights and the locks. The UI runs the part the customer touches.

mappings.ai_concept: Telemetry / instrumentation (token tracker, skill-usage logs, OB1 access counters)
mappings.punchline: A car without sensors runs blind. So does an AI stack without telemetry.

mappings.ai_concept: Monitoring + token budget + system health visibility
mappings.punchline: If you can't see the gauges, you don't know the engine's about to blow. Same with AI.
Plug in, read codes, find the problem. No guessing.
The engine doesn't run on hope. It runs on fuel. And fuel costs money.

mappings.ai_concept: Model tier (Opus vs Sonnet vs Haiku)
mappings.punchline: Premium fuel in a Civic is wasted. Regular in a race car is a misfire. Match the model to the job.
Range anxiety is real. So is rate-limit anxiety.

mappings.ai_concept: Out-of-the-box AI (raw ChatGPT, no memory, no hooks)
mappings.punchline: Stock tune is safe for the manufacturer. It's never optimal for you.
Same engine. Two completely different cars.

mappings.ai_concept: Bolted-on retrofit (Zapier on top of legacy CRM)
mappings.punchline: Piggybacks work. They also lie to the stock ECU all day. Eventually something gives.
Wrong gap, misfire. Worn out, misfire. Replace them more often than you think.
Dirty air filter and the engine chokes. Bad RAG and the agent chokes the same way.
Skip the oil change. Watch the engine seize. There's no warning, then there's no engine.
Coolant looks fine until the day it doesn't. Same with API quotas.
Old brake fluid is the day you find out the brakes don't work.
Front tires wear differently. So do your most-used skills. Rotate or lose tread.

mappings.ai_concept: Cron job audit (the thing that snaps and ruins the engine)
mappings.punchline: Timing belt snaps, valves hit pistons, engine done. Cron job snaps, the whole stack drifts and nobody knows when it broke.
Detailing doesn't make the car faster. It makes the car sellable.
